Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Flights are resuming across the country
this morning, but travelers are still dealing with the fallout from Friday's nationwide
ground stop. Passenger Kate Tuttle was traveling from Knoxville, Tennessee to Syracuse last night
for business when she realized her luggage was missing. They canceled my flight, so there's no
kind of picking that one back up. Luckily for me, I have a friend who lives in Knoxville,
so it's four hours. She's driving to get me, and then we're going to make our meetings tomorrow at
least. If I can find my luggage, that's the biggest thing now. We don't know where our luggage is.
The FAA halted departures nationwide because of problems with radar and communication systems.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says getting flights moving again will take time.
We've opened up the airspace. Now, does that mean every flight is going to fly?
Right now, it's going to be slow, right? So if you're watching, you're at an airport,
check with your airline. It depends on do we have crews available.
Aviation officials say more than 3,000 flights into or out of the United States have been
canceled today. Democrat Jonathan Christ Tompkins will be the next governor of Alaska. That's
according to a race call by the Associated Press. Eric Stone of Alaska Public Media reports will
replace outgoing Republican governor Mike Dunlavy. Better known as JKT, Christ Tompkins spent a decade
representing his hometown of Sitka as a state legislator after dropping out of Yale. Now, at 37,
he'll be the youngest governor in Alaska history and the first Democrat to lead the state since
2002. Christ Tompkins says he ran on reaching across the aisle to solve problems that have
bedeviled the state for years, from slow permitting to an underfunded school system.
We wanted to bring Alaskans together and focus on issues that unite more than they defied,
and we want to be problem solvers. He defeated three Republicans in the four-person rate choice
race, including one backed by President Trump. For NPR News, I'm Eric Stone in Juneau, Alaska.
Stocks on Wall Street gained ground this week as gasoline prices fell,
and PR Scott Horsley reports all of the major indexes rose more than 2% for the week.
Gasoline prices dipped below $4 a gallon this week for the first time in three months.
That took some of the sting out of inflation reports showing the overall cost of living
continues to climb. Wholesale prices in October were up 6.5% from a year ago, the biggest annual
increase in nearly four years. Investors expect the Federal Reserve to respond by raising interest
rates next month. Jensen Wong stepped down as CEO of the AI chip-making giant NVIDIA after
acknowledging an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The rest of the tech sector
was unscathed, however. The NASDAQ gained 2.25% for the week, while the Dow rose just over 2%,
and the S&P 500 jumped 2.5%. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR. Investigators are working to determine why a tanker struck a docked cruise
boat in New Orleans yesterday. Mayor Helena Marino describes how the evacuation turned into a rescue.
The passengers began disembarking from the ship after that collision. But while that was happening,
the cruise ship began to sink, and then eventually the cruise ship toppled over and flipped.
Now, when that occurred, we started to have people in the water.
Tugboat crews, port workers, and police helped pull passengers from the Mississippi River.
More than 30 people were taken to area hospitals to be treated for injuries.
The National Transportation Safety Board says it's planning to investigate. SpaceX has conducted
another launch of its giant Starship rocket. As NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports, the company
has a lot riding on this mission. The SpaceX rocket lifted off from its launch pad in south
Texas. Starship had a smooth ride to orbit, but its massive super-heavy booster rocket did not
make the trip back to Earth as planned. Rather than landing back at the launch site, it crashed
into the Gulf. Starship, meanwhile, went on to deploy 26 satellites for SpaceX's starling
constellation. If all goes well, it will return to the launch site where it will land at the pad.
That landing would be a key step towards making the rocket more rapidly reusable.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News. This is NPR News in Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone. Rosetta Stone is designed to make language

Passenger Kate Tuttle describes lost luggage and canceled flight from Knoxville to Syracuse
Democrat JT Christ Tompkins projected winner of Alaska governor's race, per the Associated Press
Wall Street stocks gain for the week as gasoline prices dip below $4 a gallon
Wholesale prices rise 6.5% in October, the biggest annual increase in nearly four years
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang steps down after acknowledging affair with suspected Chinese spy
